Rick Beard

Legal Marijuana NOW candidate for Governor and Lt. Governor, Nebraska · Challenger

Wine professional and private chef; runs a food and catering business in Omaha

Rick Beard, 58, of Omaha is the Legal Marijuana NOW Party's candidate for governor of Nebraska. He beat James J. Charvat III for the party's nomination in the May 12, 2026 primary and is on the November 3 general election ballot. In August 2026 he picked Keenya "Ruby" Barnes, an Omaha Housing Authority resident commissioner, as his running mate for lieutenant governor.

Where Beard stands

Medical marijuana
Proposes a medical cannabis program run by the state, in which the state hires farmers and runs facilities. Supports access for any adult with a doctor's recommendation, including smokeable products, and says the program could bring in $100M–$500M a year.
Medical marijuana
Says he wants to keep cannabis legal for medical use only, not recreational. Argues that the state Medical Cannabis Commission's rules and fees make it impossible for the voter-approved program to succeed.
Property taxes
Says new revenue from cannabis and hemp would let the state reduce property taxes and fix roads.
Government spending
To close the state budget shortfall, says Nebraska must end tax breaks for corporations and the 'ultra-rich' and must not turn away federal dollars.
Government accountability
Wants to remove corporate, special-interest and political action committee (PAC) money from Nebraska politics, and calls this a central focus of his campaign.
Economy and agriculture
Supports legalizing industrial hemp. Proposes using hemp to double Nebraska's biofuel production and to make cheaper building materials for housing.
Data centers
Proposes pausing data center development for closer review and requiring closed-loop cooling systems.
Ballot measures / voter-approved laws
Supports the Respect Nebraska Voters proposal, which would require 40 of 49 state senators to change laws passed by voters.

Background

  • Legal Marijuana NOW nominee for Nebraska governor (won May 12, 2026 primary)
  • Wine professional and private chef
  • Owned and consulted for food and wine businesses in California (Murphys area) and Nebraska
  • Started a catering company after moving back to Omaha
  • Works with a nonprofit that teaches urban food production
  • Has helped others work through legal cannabis regulations in California
